question.prompt: Construct an angle equal to a given angle using a straightedge and compass: mark off \(OC=OD=4\text{ cm}\) on the two sides of the given angle, and measure \(CD=3\text{ cm}\). On one side of the new angle, mark \(O'C'=4\text{ cm}\), then construct \(O'D'=4\text{ cm}\) and \(C'D'=CD\). What is the length of \(C'D'\) (in cm)?

solutions.explanation: When copying an angle, set \(C'D'=CD\), so the three pairs of corresponding sides are equal (SSS), and \(\triangle O'C'D'\cong\triangle OCD\). Thus, \(C'D'=3\).
solutions.title: Use the prescribed segment equality
